agent_notes: Gloss of אֵל (pos 4) corrected from STEPBible 'God' with the entity deity.yhwh: here it is the common noun 'God', parallel to יָהּ in the first colon; I keep the literal 'God' and do not flatten it to the name.

בִּרְקִיעַ עֻזּוֹ: KJV/ASV/Webster 'firmament of his power' keeps the Latin-derived 'firmament'; YLT 'expanse' is closer. Whether the possessive points to the sky as the seat of his might or to the strength he shows there is open; Ibn Ezra, Radak and Meiri read the sky/spheres, Ibn Ezra (citing Yehuda ha-Levi) the Ark. I kept both senses open in the literal layer and followed the sky in the dramatic layer.

agent_notes: Per the reviewer's request, the shofar note no longer cites Radak for the shofar/trumpet distinction; the distinction is left as a lexical point with the Targum cited only for its rendering of the word. Radak is cited only for what he says: the trumpets (חצוצרות) are included in this praise.

STEPBible glosses נֵבֶל as 'lyre' and כִּנּוֹר as 'harp'; I kept 'lute' out and rendered נֵבֶל 'harp' and כִּנּוֹר 'lyre' in the glosses, since the kinnor is the better-attested lyre and the nevel a larger, jar-shaped harp or lyre. The identification of both is not certain; the five English versions split (psaltery/harp, corded instruments).

מִנִּים is uncertain: Rashi, Metzudat Zion and Radak (who says the instrument is not known to us) do not identify it; Ibn Ezra reads it as 'many kinds, one tune'; Meiri guesses an organ. I glossed it 'strings', following the common reading (cf. Ps 45:9 [8]) and flagged it as uncertain.

agent_notes: צִלְצְלֵי־שָׁמַע / צִלְצְלֵי תְרוּעָה: Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David take both as cymbals (the second 'sounding the teruah'); Meiri and Metzudat Zion take the second as trumpets. I render 'cymbals' for both and note the dispute in the commentary.

הַנְּשָׁמָה is grammatically singular; its verb תְּהַלֵּל is the jussive-or-imperfect, 'let/shall praise'. I render 'let' in the literal layer ('let every breath praise'), a choice between a wish and a statement.

צֶלְצְלֵי־שָׁמַע / תְרוּעָה: дословно «кимвалы слуха» и «кимвалы клича»; Синодальный перевод даёт «звучные» и «громогласные» — два оттенка громкости, которых в еврейском нет.
